summary: A draft of IPng requirements from the point of view of the Cellular Digital Packet Data consortium of service providers. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo presents the Cellular Digital Packet Data consortium's proposed requirements for IPng. It emphasizes mobility, scalable addressing, security, accounting, efficient use of wireless bandwidth, and coexistence with IPv4.

subtitle: The CDPD consortium's proposed requirements for IPng.

tldr.problem: The CDPD consortium wanted IPng to support mobile devices, large address needs, and the operational requirements of wireless data services.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists requirements covering mobility, scale, addressing, security, accounting, route selection, data efficiency, and transition from IPv4.
tldr.outcome: It provides input to IPng technical discussions and explicitly does not represent an industry endorsement or commitment.

today: RFC 1674 is Informational and presents draft requirements from CDPD consortium representatives. It does not specify an Internet standard or commit the consortium or its member companies.

sections.title: Mobility for Wireless Devices
sections.content:
The memo presents draft IPng requirements from representatives of the CDPD service-provider consortium. Its primary requirement is that IPng not impede mobility: devices should operate in different locations while applications remain the same for users.

The memo says packets should be self-contained and allow redirection, so IPng should remain connectionless. It also calls for native support for mobility and for occasionally connected hosts.
sections.plainLanguage: IPng should allow a device to move without changing how its applications look to the user. The memo also says IPng should accommodate devices that connect only sometimes.

sections.title: Scale, Addressing, and Security
sections.content:
The consortium estimates 20 to 40 million North American users by 2007 and says IPng should support billions of users worldwide and tens or hundreds of billions of addresses. It expects hierarchical, variable-length addresses, distributed administration, and a mapping between names and addresses that is independent of location.

The memo also calls for security services such as peer authentication, data and traffic-flow confidentiality, data integrity, and location confidentiality. It identifies Layer 3 accounting as a requirement.
sections.plainLanguage: The consortium expects very large numbers of users and asks for flexible addresses that can be managed across organizations. It also lists security and accounting as requirements.

sections.title: Route Selection and Wireless Efficiency
sections.content: The memo says source- and policy-based inter-domain routing could support service-provider selection, and IPng should allow selection of at least the first transit provider based on the source host. It also calls for compact Layer 3 protocol information and packet prioritization to use limited wide-area wireless bandwidth efficiently.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed routing features would let traffic selection depend on the source host. The memo also asks IPng to keep overhead low and support packet priorities on limited-bandwidth networks.

sections.title: Transition from IPv4
sections.content:
The memo says IPng must interoperate with IP for the foreseeable future. It calls for bridging mechanisms and a defined transition strategy, and notes that options fields could help new protocols support IP addresses and headers.

The submission is input to IETF technical discussions; it does not represent endorsement or commitment by the CDPD consortium, cellular industry, or constituent companies.
sections.plainLanguage: IPng should work alongside IP during a transition. These requirements are a contribution to discussion, not a commitment by the organizations named.

references.text: Gross, P., ed., "IP: Next Generation (IPng) White Paper Solicitation", RFC 1550, December 1993.
